_what: Claims about jurisdictions nobody on this project monitors. Keyed by the claim, not by the number, because a figure like 5% means an agent's commission on twenty Greek pages and something else entirely abroad. Every entry needs claim, jurisdiction, source, asOf, reviewBy and the files that carry it. `npm run facts:review` fails once a reviewBy date passes and reports claims whose files have disappeared.
_why: The Greek figures on this site have a watcher: the Government Gazette, AADE circulars and the Ministry of Migration are all checkable on demand. Foreign tax rules have none, so a stale one would sit here indefinitely under an asOf date quietly asserting it was current. The R3 nationality guides rest almost entirely on foreign tax law, which is why they are registered here before anything else.
_still_unregistered: Cleared for compare/. The remaining unregistered foreign material on this site is descriptive rather than load-bearing: market colour on foreign yields and prices, which is labelled as modelled or directional in the text and is not a legal claim anybody should act on. If any of it becomes a decision input, register it here first.

claims.claim: The United States taxes citizens and green card holders on worldwide income regardless of residence, so a Greek purchase creates US filing consequences whether or not the owner spends any time in the property, and relocating to Greece does not end them.
claims.source: Internal Revenue Code; IRS guidance for US citizens and resident aliens abroad

claims.claim: The US-Greece income tax convention signed in 1950 operates on the credit method rather than the exemption method, so Greek tax on rental income is claimed as a foreign tax credit on Form 1116 and the taxpayer effectively pays the higher of the two rates.
claims.source: Convention between the United States and Greece for the avoidance of double taxation, signed 1950

claims.claim: FinCEN Form 114 is due once aggregate foreign financial accounts exceed USD 10,000 at any point in the calendar year, measured at the highest balance rather than at year end, and it is filed separately from the income tax return.
claims.source: 31 CFR 1010.350; FinCEN BSA e-filing requirements for FBAR

claims.claim: EB-5 minimum investment amounts were raised and made subject to periodic adjustment by the EB-5 Reform and Integrity Act of 2022, so comparisons quoting pre-2022 figures are stale and current USCIS minimums must be checked directly.
claims.source: EB-5 Reform and Integrity Act of 2022; USCIS EB-5 programme pages

claims.claim: Form T1135 must be filed where the total cost amount of specified foreign property exceeds CAD 100,000 at any point in the year. Reporting is on cost amount rather than market value, and the penalty regime attaches to the missing form rather than to unpaid tax.
claims.source: Income Tax Act (Canada) s.233.3; CRA Form T1135 guidance

claims.claim: Quebec residents holding more than CAD 100,000 of foreign property file Revenu Quebec form TP-1079.8.BE in addition to the federal T1135; Quebec is the only province with a separate provincial foreign-property disclosure.
claims.source: Revenu Quebec, form TP-1079.8.BE and accompanying guide

claims.claim: Ceasing Canadian tax residence triggers a deemed disposition of most property at fair market value on the departure date, and severing residence is a facts-and-circumstances test rather than an election.
claims.source: Income Tax Act (Canada) s.128.1; CRA guidance on leaving Canada

claims.claim: The Canadian principal residence exemption is not limited by geography and a property outside Canada may in principle be designated, subject to the ordinarily-inhabited test and the one-property-per-family-unit-per-year limit.
claims.source: Income Tax Act (Canada) s.40(2)(b) and s.54; CRA folio on the principal residence exemption

claims.claim: Australia and Greece have no comprehensive double taxation agreement. An Airline Profits Agreement covers the taxation of airline operations only, so there is no treaty relief, no treaty rates, no residence tie-breaker article and no mutual agreement procedure for property income.
claims.source: Australian Treasury register of tax treaties; Australia-Greece Airline Profits Agreement

claims.claim: Relief for foreign tax paid runs through the Foreign Income Tax Offset, which is capped and whose excess is not carried forward, so where the foreign charge exceeds the Australian tax on the same income the excess is lost.
claims.source: Income Tax Assessment Act 1997 (Cth) Division 770; ATO guidance on the foreign income tax offset

claims.claim: An individual is an Australian tax resident if they satisfy any of the ordinary residence, domicile, 183-day or Commonwealth superannuation tests, so spending under 183 days in Australia does not by itself end residency.
claims.source: Income Tax Assessment Act 1936 (Cth) s.6(1); ATO residency guidance

claims.claim: A self-managed superannuation fund is bound by the sole purpose test and the related-party and in-house asset rules, so a property the members or their relatives intend to use personally is not a compliant fund investment.
claims.source: Superannuation Industry (Supervision) Act 1993 (Cth) s.62 and Part 8; ATO SMSF guidance

claims.claim: Under the Reserve Bank of India's Liberalised Remittance Scheme a resident individual may remit up to USD 250,000 per financial year, the Indian financial year runs 1 April to 31 March, and unused headroom does not carry forward.
claims.source: Reserve Bank of India, Liberalised Remittance Scheme master direction

claims.claim: Tax Collected at Source applies to LRS remittances above Rs 10 lakh in a financial year at 20% for purposes other than education and medical treatment. It is creditable against Indian income tax liability and recoverable through the return, but is withheld at the point of remittance.
claims.source: Income-tax Act 1961 (India) s.206C(1G); CBDT circulars on TCS under LRS

claims.claim: Exceeding the LRS limit or structuring around it exposes the remitter to penalties under the Foreign Exchange Management Act, and remittances declared under one purpose code and applied to another attract scrutiny.
claims.source: Foreign Exchange Management Act 1999 (India); RBI A2 form and purpose code schedule

claims.claim: The United Arab Emirates levies no personal income tax on individuals and does not tax individual capital gains, so Greek tax on rental income is a final cost with no home-country credit available against it.
claims.source: UAE federal tax legislation; UAE Ministry of Finance guidance on personal taxation

claims.claim: UAE residency for most expatriates is conditional and renewable rather than permanent, tied to an employer, an investor visa or a qualifying property holding, and it ends when the underlying condition ends.
claims.source: UAE Federal Authority for Identity and Citizenship residence visa categories

claims.claim: Under the Israel-Greece double taxation treaty, income from immovable property and gains on its disposal are allocated to the state where the property is situated, so an Israeli resident's Greek rental income and disposal gains carry no second Israeli charge.
claims.source: Convention between Israel and Greece for the avoidance of double taxation, Articles 6 and 13

claims.claim: Israeli disclosure obligations attaching to foreign assets and foreign accounts are independent of whether tax is payable, so exclusive taxing rights in Greece remove the Israeli charge without removing the Israeli filing requirement.
claims.source: Israel Income Tax Ordinance reporting provisions; Israel Tax Authority guidance on foreign assets

claims.claim: Portugal's Mais Habitacao housing package, in force from October 2023, removed direct real estate purchase as a qualifying route for the Autorizacao de Residencia para Investimento. The programme continues on non-property routes; property alone no longer qualifies a new applicant.
claims.source: Portugal, Lei 56/2023 (Mais Habitacao); AIMA guidance on ARI qualifying investment categories

claims.claim: The Portuguese collective investment route requires a subscription of at least EUR 500,000 into a fund that is incorporated and headquartered in Portugal, has a maturity of at least five years, and invests at least 60 percent of its portfolio in companies headquartered in Portugal.
claims.source: Portugal, Lei 23/2007 as amended, ARI qualifying investment categories; AIMA fund route guidance

claims.claim: Portugal replaced SEF with AIMA as the immigration authority, and the transition produced multi-year processing backlogs on ARI files between 2022 and 2024. Quoted Portuguese processing times from that period do not describe the current position and must be re-checked.
claims.source: Portugal, Decreto-Lei 41/2023 establishing AIMA; AIMA public statements on the ARI backlog

claims.claim: Spain closed its property-backed Golden Visa to new applications on 3 April 2025 under Organic Law 1/2025. The route had operated since 2013 with a EUR 500,000 real estate minimum. Permits granted before that date continue and renew under their original terms.
claims.source: Spain, Ley Organica 1/2025, final provisions repealing the real estate investor residence route of Ley 14/2013

claims.claim: After the 2025 closure Spain retains non-property routes for third-country nationals: a capital investment residence requiring EUR 1,000,000 or more in Spanish company shares or public debt, the Non-Lucrative Visa evidencing passive income with no right to work, and the Digital Nomad Visa for remote workers earning from outside Spain.
claims.source: Spain, Ley 14/2013 as amended by Ley Organica 1/2025; Ministerio de Inclusion guidance on residence visa categories

claims.claim: Italy's Investor Visa under Article 26-bis of Legislative Decree 286/1998 excludes direct real estate purchase. Qualifying investments are EUR 250,000 in an innovative startup, EUR 500,000 in an Italian limited company, EUR 1,000,000 in a philanthropic donation, or EUR 2,000,000 in Italian government bonds. Buying Italian property confers no residence status.
claims.source: Italy, Decreto Legislativo 286/1998 art. 26-bis; Ministero delle Imprese e del Made in Italy, Investor Visa for Italy programme guidance

claims.claim: All-in acquisition costs on an Italian or Spanish residential purchase commonly fall between 9 and 13 percent of price, driven by regional registration or transfer tax rates, the cadastral rather than market basis of the charge in Italy, and whether a reduced first-home rate applies.
claims.source: Agenzia delle Entrate guidance on imposta di registro and prima casa relief; Spanish autonomous community ITP schedules

claims.claim: The Malta Permanent Residence Programme requires a non-refundable government contribution alongside either the purchase or the lease of qualifying property, plus an administrative fee and separate per-dependent fees. The contribution is a cost rather than an investment and is not recovered on exit, which is the structural difference from a Greek deed.
claims.source: Malta, Residency Malta Agency, Malta Permanent Residence Programme regulations and fee schedule

claims.claim: Cyprus fast-track permanent residency through property requires the purchase of a new residential unit from a developer at a stated minimum around EUR 300,000 excluding VAT, on first sale rather than resale stock, with income and deposit conditions attached separately.
claims.source: Cyprus, Regulation 6(2) of the Aliens and Immigration Regulations; Civil Registry and Migration Department criteria for the accelerated PR procedure

claims.claim: UAE property-linked residence permits are granted against eligible real estate at thresholds set federally and applied per emirate, with off-plan and mortgaged units treated differently from completed freehold. Thresholds and eligible-project rules change without notice and must be confirmed for the specific emirate and route.
claims.source: UAE Federal Authority for Identity and Citizenship; Dubai Land Department guidance on property investor residence

claims.claim: Hungary's Guest Investor Programme grants a long-term residence permit against a subscription to units in a regulated real-estate fund at a threshold marketed near EUR 250,000, rather than against direct property ownership. The investor holds fund units; the fund holds the buildings. Hungary previously ran and then closed a residency bond scheme, and reopened investment migration under separate later legislation.
claims.source: Hungary, Act XC of 2023 on the general rules for the entry and residence of third-country nationals; Hungarian government guest investor programme guidance

claims.claim: Croatia operates no residence-by-investment programme. Property ownership confers no immigration status on a third-country national, who must instead qualify for temporary stay on work, family, study or self-employment grounds judged on their own merits.
claims.source: Croatia, Zakon o strancima (Aliens Act) temporary stay categories; Ministry of the Interior residence guidance

claims.claim: Third-country nationals acquire Croatian real estate only where a reciprocity arrangement exists between Croatia and their own state, and the acquisition then requires the consent of the Croatian Ministry of Justice before title transfers. EU and EEA nationals buy on broadly the same footing as Croatian nationals, with agricultural and forest land treated separately. A Croatian d.o.o. is a domestic legal person and acquires without the consent step.
claims.source: Croatia, Zakon o vlasnistvu i drugim stvarnim pravima (Ownership and Other Real Rights Act) arts. 354-358; Ministry of Justice reciprocity list

claims.claim: Croatia charges real estate transfer tax on resale purchases, while a new build sold by a VAT-registered developer carries VAT instead of the transfer tax. Croatia also replaced its holiday-home charge with an annual real estate tax set within a statutory range by each municipality, so comparable properties in different opcine can be charged materially different amounts.
claims.source: Croatia, Zakon o porezu na promet nekretnina; Zakon o lokalnim porezima as amended for the annual real estate tax

claims.claim: South Africa grants no residence right through property purchase. Foreign buyers acquire freehold on the same footing as residents and pay the same transfer duty scale with no foreign-buyer surcharge, the scale running from a nil-rated lower band up to a top marginal band in the low teens of percent.
claims.source: South African Revenue Service transfer duty rate tables; Deeds Registries Act ownership provisions

claims.claim: South Africa gazetted a remote work visitor visa in 2024 with a gross annual income threshold of ZAR 650,796. It is a work-authorisation route unrelated to property ownership and confers no Schengen rights.
claims.source: South Africa, Immigration Regulations amendment gazetted 2024 introducing the remote working visa

claims.claim: A US person holding foreign property through a non-US company can fall within the controlled foreign corporation or passive foreign investment company regimes, which carry separate annual information returns with substantial penalties and can attribute income to the shareholder whether or not it is distributed. Direct personal ownership avoids both.
claims.source: Internal Revenue Code subpart F (ss.951-965) and ss.1291-1298; IRS instructions to Forms 5471 and 8621

claims.claim: FATCA obliges foreign financial institutions to identify and report accounts held by US persons, and the resulting compliance burden makes some non-US banks slower to onboard American customers. Form 8938 reporting by the individual is separate from the FBAR and applies different thresholds.
claims.source: Internal Revenue Code ch.4 (ss.1471-1474); IRS Form 8938 instructions

claims.claim: US states are not parties to federal income tax treaties and do not necessarily follow their allocation of taxing rights, so a resident of a state taxing worldwide income can face a state charge that the federal foreign tax credit does not relieve.
claims.source: US state income tax statutes; federal treaty practice on subnational taxes

claims.claim: Canada levies no inheritance tax. On death the deceased is treated as having disposed of capital property at fair market value immediately before death, so the accrued gain is taxed on the final return of the deceased rather than charged to the heirs. Greek inheritance tax falls on each heir and is computed on the value of their share, so the two charges have different taxpayers and different bases and generally do not relieve one another.
claims.source: Income Tax Act (Canada) s.70(5); CRA guidance on the final return of a deceased person

claims.claim: Foreign real property is not a qualified investment for an RRSP, TFSA or RRIF, so a Canadian buying property abroad does so with after-tax money outside every registered plan.
claims.source: Income Tax Act (Canada) s.207.01 and Regulation 4900; CRA folio on qualified investments

claims.claim: The Australian income year runs 1 July to 30 June while Greece taxes on the calendar year, so a single Australian year draws on two Greek tax years and the Australian return frequently falls due before the overlapping Greek assessment is final. The Foreign Income Tax Offset is claimed on foreign tax finally assessed rather than on amounts withheld.
claims.source: Income Tax Assessment Act 1997 (Cth) Division 770 and s.4-10; ATO guidance on the foreign income tax offset and on foreign currency translation

claims.claim: A resident individual must disclose foreign assets in the foreign assets schedule of the Indian income tax return every year, whether or not the asset produces income and whether or not tax is payable. A resident is also taxed in India on worldwide capital gains, so a gain on foreign property is reportable in India even where the source country charges nothing.
claims.source: Income-tax Act 1961 (India) s.5 and s.139; Schedule FA of the Indian income tax return; Black Money (Undisclosed Foreign Income and Assets) Act 2015

claims.claim: Israel grants new immigrants and returning residents a multi-year exemption from Israeli tax on foreign-source income and gains on foreign assets, running from the date Israeli residence begins or resumes, and its scope has extended to reporting as well as to tax. The relief ends on a fixed date, its reporting scope has been subject to legislative change, and eligibility is determined on the facts of when residence began.
claims.source: Israel Income Tax Ordinance, relief for new immigrants and returning residents introduced by Amendment 168 (2008); Israel Tax Authority guidance

claims.claim: The UAE federal corporate tax applies to businesses and to natural persons carrying on business activity above a turnover threshold, while personal investment income and personal real estate investment held by an individual fall outside its scope. Holding foreign property through a UAE company or free-zone entity therefore places the holder inside a regime an individual owner is not in.
claims.source: UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 47 of 2022 on the Taxation of Corporations and Businesses; UAE Ministry of Finance guidance on natural persons

claims.claim: Hungary is a member of the European Union and is not in the eurozone, so a Hungarian real-estate fund's assets and unit price sit in the Hungarian economy. The subscription currency, the currency in which net asset value is calculated and any hedging policy are matters for the fund documentation rather than for the programme's rules.
claims.source: EU member state currency arrangements; Hungarian collective investment fund disclosure requirements

claims.claim: Croatia grants a temporary stay permit to third-country nationals working remotely for employers outside Croatia, alongside the ordinary work, family reunification, study and self-employment categories. Each is granted and maintained on its own conditions and none is supported by owning Croatian property. Croatia is in Schengen, so a visitor's days there and in Greece draw on the same 90-in-180 allowance.
claims.source: Croatia, Zakon o strancima (Aliens Act) temporary stay categories including digital nomads; Schengen Borders Code short-stay rules
